subject: Request: soft-reserve GPUs + latency-credit addendum for NebulaCorp
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@nebulacorp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@nebulacorp.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity - soft reservation request and SLA carveout

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier — NebulaCorp has been seeing significant tail latency during our nightly batch inference windows (short spikes ~20-30 minutes). We run a mixed workload: steady low-latency user traffic plus predictable batch jobs that push concurrent token throughput. Even with a dedicated pool configured, we get intermittent 99th-percentile latency breaches that hit our SLAs with our customers.

We wanted to discuss two things: (1) whether Redwood can offer a "soft-reserve" reservation model (a small guaranteed headroom on a dedicated pool that is only used for our jobs unless capacity is tight), and (2) a structure of latency credits — i.e., if Redwood cannot meet the agreed p95/p99 windows during those windows, we receive a creditable offset on our invoice rather than a full service termination.

Attached is a short PDF with our traffic profile, expected qps, payload sizes, and retention constraints. Can you outline what options exist, and what a pilot would look like (config, metrics, price delta)? We are hoping to run a 4–6 week pilot to validate behavior.

Appreciate any details you can share.

—Samir
Samir Patel | CTO, NebulaCorp
Attachments: nebulacorp_service_requirements.pdf (PDF, 73KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - soft reservation request and SLA carveout

Samir — thanks for the detailed note and the profile. We can definitely make space to run a pilot and explore a formal addendum. High level options we usually evaluate:

- Hard reserved capacity: exclusive nodes for NebulaCorp (higher cost, lowest tail risk).
- Soft-reserve / priority scheduling: a small number of GPUs that carry higher scheduling weight for your tenant but can be preempted with bounded grace if global emergencies occur.
- Latency-credit arrangement: define p50/p95/p99 thresholds with a credit schedule for breaches during agreed windows.

To scope the pilot we need: peak QPS and average sequence length during your batch windows, KV cache hit rate, and whether you need sticky worker affinity for KV cache locality. If you can confirm those numbers I'll loop in Jonas (runtime) for the technical proposal and Ben for pricing / term tradeoffs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-min technical alignment call this week (Jonas to run through queueing/preemption behavior).
2) Draft a pilot addendum (we can re-use a template) that includes: pilot length (4 weeks), soft-reserve config (3 GPUs, priority band), observable SLOs and credit table.
3) Ben will propose a pilot price and longer-term commit discounts if pilot looks good.

I attached a draft addendum skeleton for transparency — we'll fill in specifics after the call. When are you available for the call?

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
"draft-addendum-20261111.docx" attached
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@nebulacorp.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - soft reservation request and SLA carveout

LAURA / BEN — quick technical notes so we can be concrete on the call. Copying Samir for visibility.

Summary of how soft-reserve would behave in our runtime:
- We create a priority band for NebulaCorp jobs. Requests in that band are placed ahead of standard work but behind any "emergency" platform-level traffic.
- We hold N GPUs in that band as soft headroom; they are not exclusive — they are just weighted higher by scheduler.
- Preemption policy: we implement bounded preemption where the in-flight generation is allowed to finish a configurable grace window (we typically use 100–250ms to drain the token pipeline) before preemption. Long-running batch tasks are chunked to avoid large preemption penalties.
- To reduce tail latency we can enable sticky worker affinity for KV cache sessions (hits stay on the same worker) and use adaptive batching thresholds for your batch window so we keep latency predictable.

Proposed pilot config (conservative):
- soft_reserve_gpus: 3
- priority_weight: high (x1.8 scheduling multiplier)
- preemption_grace_ms: 200
- headroom_target: 20% (target unused capacity reserved for bursts)
- observe metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, queue depth, preemption count, eviction rate

If NebulaCorp needs strict exclusivity during a daily 30-minute window, we'd need to switch to hard reserved nodes or schedule a dedicated time-sliced window to avoid cross-tenant risk.

Happy to walk through these on the call and show a simulated trace.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@nebulacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - soft reservation request and SLA carveout

Laura / team — a few commercial points to add before we present to procurement at Nebula: 

- Pilot pricing: for the 4-week pilot with 3 soft-reserve GPUs we can do a reduced pilot rate (50% of committed reserved price).
- Long-term: if Nebula commits to a 6-month reserved capacity + soft-reserve carveout, we can offer a 10–18% discount depending on total GPU months.
- Credits: recommend a tiered credit table tied to p99 breaches during the agreed windows (e.g., 0.5% credit per breach up to a cap). Legal will need to sign a short addendum that defines measurement windows and remediation.

I'll prepare an MLP (mutual action plan) with deadlines and a simple pricing sheet. Also propose we include a one-time credit ($25k) for migration validation if Nebula signs a 6-month commit.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - soft reservation request and SLA carveout

Samir — great sync today. Recap and next steps so we all have the same plan: 

1) Pilot: 4 weeks starting on your sign-off date. Config: 3 soft-reserve GPUs, priority_weight x1.8, preemption_grace 200ms, headroom target 20%. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, queue depth, preemption_count.
2) Commercials: pilot at 50% of reserved pilot rate; conditional $25k migration validation credit if Nebula executes a 6-month commit within 30 days of pilot finish.
3) Legal: we'll draft a short addendum that defines the latency credit table and measurement windows. Ben will coordinate the pricing sheet and the DocuSign when draft is approved.
4) Action items:
   - Samir: confirm peak QPS and average seq len for the nightly batch window (file attached shows our understanding).
   - Jonas: produce a short runbook describing preemption behavior and observability hooks.
   - Ben: generate MLP and pricing, push an editable addendum to DocuSign.

I've attached the mutual action plan and the draft addendum. If that looks good I'll get legal to iterate on the wording around credits (we try to avoid open-ended SLAs but will be explicit about measurement and caps).

Proposed times for pilot kickoff call: Thu 11/12 10:00 or Fri 11/13 09:00 PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
